findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when TopicUser row does not exist
findings.body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb TopicsController#unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) and then immediately dereferences tu.notification_level and tu.save!. A user who was never tracked on the topic, e.g. notified via mailing-list mode or group, has no TopicUser row, so tu is nil and the request raises NoMethodError on nil instead of unsubscribing.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe performed on GET without CSRF protection
findings.body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb TopicsController#unsubscribe mutates notification_level and saves, but it is routed as GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and t/:topic_id/unsubscribe in config/routes.rb. GET requests are not checked for CSRF tokens, so any third-party page/image can force a logged-in user's browser to downgrade that topic's notification level, and crawlers/prefetchers can trigger it accidentally.

findings.title: Unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change callbacks and reason tracking
findings.body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb the action assigns tu.notification_level directly and calls tu.save! instead of TopicUser.change. That skips setting notifications_changed_at/notifications_reason_id, skips MessageBus notification_level_change publishing done in TopicUser.change, and skips validation of the level, leaving clients and tracking state out of sync.

findings.title: New unsubscribe_link template requires unsubscribe_url for all emails
findings.body: config/locales/server.en.yml changed unsubscribe_link to require %{unsubscribe_url}, and lib/email/message_builder.rb interpolates it in body and html_part whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. Any email built with add_unsubscribe_link:true but without unsubscribe_url in template_args will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument / render a broken link, so all current and future callers must supply it and there is no fallback.
